walkthrough:
Write the sum formula for $n$ terms of an arithmetic progression with $a = -12$ and $d = 6$:
$$S_n = \frac{n}{2}\left(2(-12) + (n - 1)6\right) = \frac{n}{2}(-24 + 6n - 6) = \frac{n}{2}(6n - 30) = 3n^2 - 15n$$

Set the inequality $S_n > 3000$ and rearrange into standard quadratic form:
$$3n^2 - 15n > 3000 \implies 3(n^2 - 5n - 1000) > 0 \implies n^2 - 5n - 1000 > 0$$

Find the positive root of the quadratic equation:
$$n = \frac{5 + \sqrt{(-5)^2 - 4(1)(-1000)}}{2} = \frac{5 + \sqrt{25 + 4000}}{2} = \frac{5 + \sqrt{4025}}{2} \approx \frac{5 + 63.443}{2} \approx 34.22$$

Since $n$ must be an integer, round up to the next integer:
$$\text{Least possible value of } n = 35$$

ai_rubric.AP Sum Inequality: Sets up $S_n > 3000$ (M1). Forms $n^2 - 5n - 1000 > 0$ (A1). Finds critical boundary $\approx 34.2$ (A1). Obtains $n = 35$ (A1).
